files.lesson.md: --- order: 4 unit: statistics node: AC9M7ST02 n1 uses: [AC9M7ST01 n2] # reading the median, mode and range from the plot title: Stem-and-leaf plots summary: "A stem-and-leaf plot keeps every value and shows the shape: the tens are the stems, the units are the leaves, written in order. Include every stem, even with no leaves, and add a key." language: maths voice: { name: af_heart, speed: 1.1 } hook: "Thirty homework times in a list tell you very little. Sort them into a stem-and-leaf plot and the shape jumps out, and you can still read every value." connection: timetable-stem-leaf # data/connections/maths.yml (documentation only) app: command: node "$REPO_ROOT/tools/serve.mjs" "$REPO_ROOT/dist/_playground-board" 8182 url: http://127.0.0.1:8182/index.html readySelector: "#gsum" layout: full explainPicture: { ref: data.yml#explain, caption: "Stems are the tens, leaves the units, in order: 3 | 1 5 5 8 is 31, 35, 35 and 38." } explainClip: query: { code: "@data.yml#explain", fresh: 1, id: explain } caption: "Tens as stems, units as leaves" say: "Tens are the stems; units are the leaves." clip: - caption: { text: "Each row is a stem (the tens). Its leaves are the units.", say: "Each row is a stem: the tens digit. The leaves are the units." } - wait: 1000 - caption: { text: "3 | 1 5 5 8 means 31, 35, 35 and 38, in order.", say: "Three, then one, five, five, eight: thirty one, thirty five, thirty five, thirty eight." } - wait: 1000 - caption: { text: "Every value is still there, and the shape shows where most of them are.", say: "Every value is kept, and the shape shows where most of them are." } - wait: 1400 --- A **stem-and-leaf plot** is a display that keeps every value. ## Predict: read a row ```step stage: predict insight: "Committing to what a row means before building one tests whether they combine the stem and each leaf into one value." check: type: predict q: "In a stem-and-leaf plot, a row reads $3 \\mid 1\\ 5\\ 5\\ 8$. Which values does it show?" options: - "31, 35, 35 and 38" - "3, 1, 5, 5 and 8" - "The number 31 558" - "3, 15 and 58" actual: "31, 35, 35 and 38. The stem 3 is the tens; each leaf is the units of one value." ``` How many values are in that row? ## Run: add two values ```step stage: run insight: "Adding values and watching them land in the right row, in order, shows the plot's rule: the tens choose the row, the units the place." try: { playground: board, starter: "data.yml#run", height: 600 } check: { type: board, text: "Add 44 and 29 to the data (type them in the box). Where does each go? Was your prediction right about reading a row?", when: "n = 10 and s = 375" } ``` The dot plot and the stem-and-leaf plot show the same data. Which is easier to read exact values from? For two-digit numbers: - the **stem** is the tens digit, written once down the left; - the **leaves** are the units digits, written in order along each stem's row; - a **key** says how to read it: $3 \mid 5$ means $35$. Turned on its side, it looks like a bar graph, so you can see the shape of the data and still read every value. ## Investigate: build and read ```step stage: investigate insight: "Stems in order with none missed, leaves in order, a key; then the median, mode and range read straight off. Jo's mistake leaves out a stem with no leaves, which hides a gap." tasks: - picture: { ref: data.yml#pic-a, caption: "A stem-and-leaf plot of 11 values." } check: type: answer q: "What is the median of the data in this plot?" answer: "27" feedback: - ["23", "23 is the mode. Count to the 6th value of 11."] - ["30", "Count carefully: 14, 18, 21, 23, 23, 27 is the 6th."] explain: "11 values, so the median is the 6th: 14, 18, 21, 23, 23, 27." - check: type: bug code: "working.txt#jo" text: "Jo draws a stem-and-leaf plot. Click the line where her working goes wrong." answer: 3 fault: logic misconception: stem-skip-empty explain: "Line 3: every stem from the smallest to the largest goes in, even with no leaves: 1, 2, 3, 4. The empty 3 row shows the gap between the 20s and the 40s." - picture: { ref: data.yml#pic-a, caption: "The same plot." } check: type: answer q: "What is the range of the data?" answer: "31" feedback: - ["41", "The lowest value is 14 (1 | 4), not 4."] - ["4", "Read whole values: highest 45, lowest 14."] explain: "Highest 45, lowest 14: 45 − 14 = 31." ``` ### Build, then read Here is how to build one, and read from it. ```worked 23, 31, 35, 35, 38, 42, 47, 51 :: Sort the values first (or sort the leaves at the end). \text{stems: } 2, 3, 4, 5 :: The tens digits, from smallest to largest, none missed out. 3 \mid 1\ 5\ 5\ 8 :: Each value's units digit goes on its stem's row, in order. \text{Key: } 3 \mid 5 = 35 :: A key says how to read the plot. \text{median} = \tfrac{35 + 38}{2} = 36.5 :: 8 values: count in to the 4th and 5th leaves. ``` Now read the median of the plot in the picture. ### Find the mistake Read Jo's working. Which stem is missing, and why does it matter? ### Range from the plot ## Modify: one change at a time ```step stage: modify insight: "One change at a time: build a plot on the board, read the mode from a different plot, count the values, use the key, then the edge case of three-digit values." try: { playground: board, starter: "data.yml#build", height: 560 } tasks: - starter: "data.yml#build" hint: "Type the values in the box: 8, 15, 17, 22, 26, 26, 31." check: { type: board, text: "Build the stem-and-leaf plot for these quiz scores: $8, 15, 17, 22, 26, 26, 31$.", when: "n = 7 and s = 145 and l = 8 and h = 31", explain: "Stems 0, 1, 2, 3: 0 | 8, 1 | 5 7, 2 | 2 6 6, 3 | 1. A one-digit value has stem 0." } - picture: { ref: data.yml#pic-b, caption: "Another stem-and-leaf plot." } check: type: answer q: "What is the mode?" answer: "63" feedback: - ["3", "Read the whole value: stem 6, leaf 3."] - ["6", "The mode is a value: the stem 6 and the repeated leaf 3 make 63."] explain: "The leaf 3 appears three times on the 6 stem: 63." - picture: { ref: data.yml#pic-b, caption: "The same plot." } check: type: answer q: "How many values are in this plot?" answer: "10" feedback: - ["3", "Count the leaves, not the stems."] explain: "Each leaf is one value: 2 + 5 + 3 = 10." - check: type: question q: "A plot of heights has the key $15 \\mid 2 = 152$ cm. What does $16 \\mid 7$ show?" options: ["167 cm", "16.7 cm", "1.67 cm"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "Use the key: 15 | 2 means 152.", "Use the key: 15 | 2 means 152."] explain: "The key tells you the place values: 16 | 7 is 167 cm." - check: type: question q: "Edge case: values $105, 112, 118, 121$. What are the stems?" options: ["10, 11 and 12", "1 only", "0, 1, 2"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "One stem of 1 would crowd every value into one row.", "The leaves are the units; the stems are everything before them."] explain: "For three-digit values the stem is the first two digits: 10 | 5, 11 | 2 8, 12 | 1." ``` ### Build one Each task changes one thing. ### The mode ### Count the values ### Use the key ### Three digits ## Practise: read the plot ```step stage: practise insight: "Reading the median, range and number of values from plots, mixed; the missing-stem slip in a question; the review keeps the mean fresh." tasks: - picture: { ref: data.yml#pic-b, caption: "A stem-and-leaf plot." } check: type: answer q: "What is the median?" answer: "63" feedback: - ["68", "10 values: the median is halfway between the 5th and 6th, both 63."] explain: "5th and 6th values are both 63, so the median is 63." - picture: { ref: data.yml#pic-b, caption: "The same plot." } check: type: answer q: "What is the range?" answer: "27" feedback: - ["7", "Use whole values: 79 − 52."] explain: "79 − 52 = 27." smaller: check: { type: number, q: "A row of a plot reads $4 \\mid 1\\ 6\\ 8$. What is the biggest value in that row?", answer: 48, tolerance: 0, feedback: [[8, "That's only the leaf. What's the stem?"]], explain: "The stem 4 is the tens and the leaf 8 is the units: 48. Read the range from whole values like this." } - check: type: question q: "Values $41, 44, 62, 65$. Which stems should the plot have?" options: ["4, 5 and 6 (5 has no leaves)", "4 and 6", "1, 2, 4 and 5"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "Leaving out 5 hides the gap in the data.", "The stems are the tens digits."] explain: "Every stem from 4 to 6, so the empty 5 row shows the gap." - check: type: answer q: "Review: find the mean of $23, 31, 35, 35$." answer: "31" feedback: - ["124", "That is the total. Divide by 4."] explain: "124 ÷ 4 = 31." ``` ### Median ### Range ### Which stems ### Review: mean ## Make: a plot with a given median ```step stage: make insight: "Building eight two-digit values with a median of 35 reverses reading: the 4th and 5th leaves must average 35." try: { playground: board, starter: "data.yml#make", height: 600 } hint: ["8 values: the median is halfway between the 4th and 5th.", "Make the 4th and 5th values 34 and 36, or 35 and 35."] check: { type: board, text: "Make a stem-and-leaf plot of 8 two-digit values with a median of 35.", when: "n = 8 and d = 35 and l >= 10", explain: "For example 21, 28, 33, 34, 36, 40, 45, 52: the 4th and 5th are 34 and 36, halfway is 35." } ``` Then: could you do it with no value of 35 at all? ## Make: on paper ```step stage: make insight: "Reading a made-up bus timetable as a stem-and-leaf plot, with the reason for counting leaves picked at the key step." check: type: reasoning paper: true q: "A bus stop's timetable is a stem-and-leaf plot (made up): the stem is the hour and the leaves are the minutes. Row 7 has leaves 05, 20, 35 and 50. Row 8 has 10, 25 and 40. Row 9 has 00 and 30. How many buses leave from 7 am up to 9 am, not counting 9:00? Draw the plot on paper first." steps: - ["Row 7 reads 7:05, 7:20, 7:35 and 7:50", "stem is the hour, each leaf is the minutes of one bus"] - ["Row 8 reads 8:10, 8:25 and 8:40", "the same way"] - ["$4 + 3 = 7$ buses", "count the leaves in rows 7 and 8; row 9 is 9:00 and later"] picks: - step: 3 q: "Why count leaves, not stems?" options: ["Each leaf is one bus; the stem only says the hour", "Each stem is one bus", "Add the stem and leaf values to get the number of buses"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "Row 7 has four buses but only one stem.", "The stem and leaf make a time, not a count."] answer: "7" answerLabel: "Buses" tolerance: 0 feedback: - ["2", "That counts the stems. Each leaf is one bus."] - ["9", "That counts every leaf, including row 9. Stop before 9:00."] criteria: - "I drew the stems in order with a key." - "I counted leaves, not stems." - "I left out row 9." explain: "Rows 7 and 8 hold 4 + 3 = 7 leaves, so 7 buses leave before 9 am." ``` Do this one in your book or on paper, one step per line, before you type the number. **Also used in** - **Timetables.** A stop's printed timetable is a stem-and-leaf plot: the hour is the stem, the minutes are the leaves. - **Sport and results.** A short list of times or scores sorts into a plot that shows the middle. - **Class work.** Sort your class's data into a plot and read its median. ```teacher summary: Students build ordered stem-and-leaf plots (tens as stems, units as leaves, every stem included, with a key) and read values, the median, mode and range from them (AC9M7ST02, node 1). time: 40 timing: Predict and Run 8 min · Investigate 12 min · Modify 12 min · Practise and Make 8 min goals: - I can build an ordered stem-and-leaf plot with a key. - I can read values, the median, the mode and the range from a stem-and-leaf plot. struggle: Reading a leaf as a value on its own, and skipping a stem with no leaves. Ask them to say the whole number aloud (3 and 1 make 31) and to write every stem in order. before: > Do the Run board first. Students need Mean, median, mode and range. This is a hinge: describing and comparing distributions (next lesson) reads shape from these plots. The common mistake is leaving out a stem with no leaves, which hides gaps; it is planted in Jo's working. Others: unordered leaves, and reading a leaf as a value on its own (the board's key helps). The board shows the dot plot and the stem-and-leaf plot together in Run and Make, so students can see they show the same data. running: - "Predict: take a show of hands; students who chose 3, 1, 5, 5, 8 read digits, not values." - "Run: ask where 29 goes and why it goes at the end of its row." - "Investigate: build a plot of the class's own data (arm spans, say) on the board." - "Modify: before the three-digit task, ask what the stems should be for 105." - "Make: collect answers; ask whether 35 has to appear." - "Paper: students draw the timetable plot in their books first; the page marks the count and the reason for counting leaves, then shows a model. Books out." stuck: - see: A student leaves out an empty stem (Jo's mistake). ask: Are there any tens between your smallest and largest stems with no values? fix: Write every stem in order; leave its row empty. - see: A student reads a leaf as a value. ask: What does the key say 3 | 5 means? fix: Stem and leaf together make one value. - see: A student writes leaves out of order. ask: Can you find the median easily from this row? fix: Sort the values first, or the leaves at the end. stretch: Draw a back-to-back stem-and-leaf plot for two classes' scores (leaves going left for one, right for the other). support: Sort the values first, then write them in rows by tens before making the plot. leads: > Next: Comparing data sets (AC9M7ST02 nodes 2 and 3). Where it leads: back-to-back plots, histograms and grouped data (Year 8 and 9). exit: q: Draw a stem-and-leaf plot of 17, 25, 22, 41, 18, 29, 26 and find its median. a: "1 | 7 8, 2 | 2 5 6 9, 3 | (empty), 4 | 1. Median: the 4th of 7 values, 25." explain: > A **stem-and-leaf plot** keeps every value and shows the shape. For two-digit numbers the **stem** is the tens digit and the **leaf** is the units digit; leaves go in order along their stem's row. Include every stem from the smallest to the largest, even with no leaves, and give a key: $3 \mid 5$ means $35$. Read the median by counting leaves to the middle; the range is the last value minus the first. ```
